Title: Senile Purpura: Up To 30% of Adults Over 75 Get These Bruises

Description:
No memory of bumping anything, but there's a dark bruise on your arm? Senile purpura affects up to 30% of adults over 75 — dark, well-defined bruises that show up mostly on the hands and forearms.

Three things make it worse: years of cumulative sun exposure that breaks down collagen, blood thinners like aspirin that let vessels bleed longer once they tear, and dry skin that's lost its elasticity.

The good news — these bruises usually fade within one to three weeks and leave no scar. Cover up with long sleeves or sunscreen before heading outside, keep track of your medications and check with your doctor if bruising gets frequent, and moisturize daily (a 12-week study found daily retinol cream actually thickened skin and boosted collagen).
